diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item We will also show that, under specific domain decomposition parameters, in addition to scalability, the one-level Schwarz method can also achieve robustness with respect of the wavenumber.

Finally, let us mention that this time, the limit spectrum is less than one (in modulus) which shows that the iterative Schwarz algorithm will converge with a rate independent of the number of domains and hence we have weak scalability.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and the contribution list promise a demonstration of robustness with respect to the wavenumber (convergence uniform in k). The body contains nothing of the kind: the analysis is mode-by-mode at fixed k, and the only numerical experiments use the two fixed values k=10 and k=10+i, concluding weak scalability (uniformity in the number of subdomains N), not k-robustness. No k-uniform estimate, k-sweep, or any statement about varying k appears anywhere. The promised demonstration is simply not in the source.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the one-level Schwarz method can achieve robustness with respect to the wave number under specific domain decomposition parameters, offering new insights into its applicability for large-scale electromagnetic wave problems.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add a genuine wavenumber-robustness analysis or numerical study (new work), or delete/soften the robustness sentences in the abstract and contribution list, withdrawing that advertised capability.
issues.overall_effect: An advertised contribution (wavenumber robustness of the one-level Schwarz method) is unsupported; the reader cannot conclude anything about the method's behavior as k varies.
issues.title: Advertised wavenumber-robustness demonstration is absent from the paper
issues.why_classification: Preserving the claim requires new nontrivial analysis or experiments, more than a routine fix; withdrawing it loses an advertised guarantee. The core framework (modal analysis, iteration matrices, limiting spectrum) is untouched, so the loss is limited rather than major.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction states as fact that Section sec:numeric presents results on the discretised problem using the edge element method, and the section's own preamble announces a second type of results on discretised Maxwell's equations. The section in fact contains only spectral-radius computations of the continuous-level iteration matrices I^T(r); there are no edge-element discretizations and no experiments on any discretised problem anywhere in the source. The announced second type of results is entirely absent.

failure_location.quote: Finally in \Cref{sec:numeric} we present two types of numerical results: first, showing that the limiting spectrum is descriptive for the convergence of the algorithm even in the case of a moderate number of domains and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For instance, $\beta^{\rm TE}_i$ will be replaced by $\beta^{\rm TE}(r) = \sqrt{k^2 - r^2}$.

issues.failure_explanation: With the eigenproblem as stated in eq:ev (-\Delta \varphi^\mathcal{N} = \lambda^\mathcal{N} \varphi^\mathcal{N}), the mode ansatz in pb:hx-modes forces k^2-\beta^2 to equal the eigenvalue itself, i.e. \beta_i = \sqrt{k^2-\lambda_i}. The paper instead defines \beta^{\rm TE}_i = \sqrt{k^2-(\lambda^\mathcal{N})_i^2} and \beta^{\rm TM}_i = \sqrt{k^2-(\lambda^\mathcal{D})_i^2}. As written, the functions e^{\pm\imath\beta_i x}\varphi_i do not satisfy pb:ex-modes/pb:hx-modes (unless \lambda_i=\lambda_i^2), so the claimed modes are not Maxwell solutions and the modal decomposition modal-dec is not a decomposition into solutions. The paper's own proof of prop:non-depend-pm confirms the intended unsquared relation: the recovery formulas have denominators \lambda^\mathcal{N}_i = k^2-\beta^2, not \lambda_i^2. The numerical parametrization \beta(r)=\sqrt{k^2-r^2} is consistent only if r replaces \sqrt{\lambda_i}, not the eigenvalue \lambda_i as the text says.

failure_location.quote: e^{\imath m \beta_i^{\rm TE} x} \varphi^\mathcal{N}_i(y,z) \quad \text{where}  \quad \beta^{\rm TE}_i = \sqrt{k^2 - (\lambda^\mathcal{N})^2_i}, \;\; i\in \mathbb{N}^+, \;\; m \in \{-,+\},

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious squares in the \beta^{\rm TE}_i and \beta^{\rm TM}_i definitions and state in the numerics that r replaces \sqrt{\lambda_i}; equivalently, restate the eigenproblems as -\Delta\varphi = \lambda^2\varphi and adjust the denominators in the proof of prop:non-depend-pm. Either repair is small and leaves every subsequent result unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The definitions of the TE/TM modal wavenumbers are internally inconsistent with the stated eigenproblems, and the numerical section's identification of r with the eigenvalues is off by a square; all results stated purely in terms of \beta^{\rm T}_i (iteration matrices, limiting spectrum) are unaffected once the definition is corrected.
issues.title: Modal wavenumbers defined with squared cross-section eigenvalue, contradicting the stated eigenproblems
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local definitional fix (with a small, equally local alternative), after which the method, all theorems, rates and advertised scope survive unchanged; no new argument or reoptimization is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: As \ell\to+\infty, the eigenvalues in eq:lambdaPML reduce to \lambda^{\rm TE}_i = -\imath\beta^{\rm TE}_i, \lambda^{\rm TM}_i = -\imath k^2/\beta^{\rm TM}_i, \lambda^{\rm TEM}_i = -\imath k, i.e. \lambda^{\rm T}_i = -\kappa for the \kappa of prop:R-ite (\imath\beta^{\rm TE}, \imath k^2/\beta^{\rm TM}, \imath k) — not +\kappa as the statement claims. Substituting \lambda=-\kappa into the b-formula of prop:R-ite gives b^{\rm T}_i = e^{+\imath\beta^{\rm T}_i(L+\delta)}; the stated value e^{-\imath\beta^{\rm T}_i(L+\delta)} corresponds to the wrong sign \lambda=+\kappa and is physically inconsistent with transparency (it grows like e^{|\beta|(L+\delta)} for evanescent modes and gives the wrong phase for propagating ones). The proof compounds this: its listed limiting eigenvalues miss factors of \imath relative to eq:lambdaPML, and its stated reason '\kappa = \lambda^{\rm T}_i' is false (the correct relation is \kappa = -\lambda^{\rm T}_i). The conclusion a^{\rm T}_i = 0 nevertheless holds, since a \propto (\lambda^2-\kappa^2), and the nilpotency argument only uses a=0, so the main claim [I^{\rm T}(i)]^N = 0 and the advertised convergence in N iterations remain valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thanks to \cref{rem:coef-TE-TM-eq}, we thus deduce that the limiting spectrum is the same for iteration matrices $I^{\rm{TE}}(r)$, $I^{\rm{TEM}}(r)$ and $I^{\rm{TM}}(r)$ since $\beta^{\rm TE}(r) = \beta^{\rm TM}(r)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Read as a statement about the actual modal wavenumbers of a rectangular waveguide, the claim is false: the Neumann spectrum (TE modes) contains eigenvalues \pi^2(m^2/L_y^2+n^2/L_z^2) with m=0 or n=0 (including the fundamental TE_{10} mode) that have no Dirichlet counterpart, since Dirichlet modes require m,n\ge 1. Hence the sets \{\beta^{\rm TE}_i\} and \{\beta^{\rm TM}_i\} do not coincide for a rectangle. The coincidence is only trivially true at the level of the artificial continuous parameter r, and the genuine justification for the TE/TM limiting-spectrum coincidence is rem:coef-TE-TM-eq, not any spectrum equality.

failure_location.quote: we will evaluate the spectral radius of the iteration matrices $I^{\rm{TE}}(r)$, $I^{\rm{TEM}}(r)$ and $I^{\rm{TM}}(r)$ since $\beta^{\rm TE}(r) = \beta^{\rm TM}(r)$ for a rectangular waveguide

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the phrase 'for a rectangular waveguide' or restate that the common parametrization is at the level of the continuous variable r only; nothing else needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: A false supporting claim about rectangular-waveguide spectra; no numerical or theoretical result is affected, since the continuous-r sweep covers all modes regardless and the real justification used is rem:coef-TE-TM-eq.
